For 2004–05, restructuring of the Serbo-Montenegrin football league system saw the dissolution of the [national second league](/wiki/Second_League_of_Serbia_and_Montenegro "Second League of Serbia and Montenegro"), instead being replaced by two regional divisions for both republics of the union with promotion to the still-united First League.

Montenegrin teams which played in European competitions during Yugoslav era were FK Budućnost, FK Sutjeska and FK Zeta.

### After independence

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Montenegrin_First_League&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: After independence")]

In 2006, after the [Independence referendum](/wiki/Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), Montenegro split from Serbia. Following that, Montenegrin First League is founded as top-tier national competition. On inaugural season, members of League became three teams from former First League of Serbia and Montenegro, seven from Second League, and two from [Montenegrin Republic League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin Republic League").

Between 2006 and 2017, the league consisted on 12 clubs, which played 33 matches during the season. From the [2017-18 season](/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_Montenegrin_First_League "2017–18 Montenegrin First League") the number of participants in the Montenegrin First League was reduced to 10, with a 36 week-long competition.

20 clubs have participated in the Montenegrin First League. The most successful are FK Sutjeska with five titles and FK Budućnost five national titles too. FK Rudar and FK Mogren won two titles. Other winners were FK Zeta and OFK Titograd with one title.

#### 2006–16

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Montenegrin_First_League&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2006–16")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/0/0e/T-com_Prva_CFL.gif)](/wiki/File:T-com_Prva_CFL.gif)

Official logo 2007–2018

The first game in Prva CFL was played on 11 August 2006 in [Pljevlja](/wiki/Pljevlja "Pljevlja"). In front of 5,000 spectators, a game between the home side [FK Rudar](/wiki/FK_Rudar_Pljevlja "FK Rudar Pljevlja") and [FK Budućnost](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"), finished with a victory of the away team (0-2). In the fifth minute of that match, [Ivan Čarapić](/w/index.php?title=Ivan_%C4%8Carapi%C4%87&action=edit&redlink=1 "Ivan Čarapić (page does not exist)") (Budućnost) scored the first goal in the history of Prva CFL.

The [first champion](/wiki/2006%E2%80%9307_Montenegrin_First_League "2006–07 Montenegrin First League") of the top-tier CFL was [Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta"), who won the trophy on the championship's final weekend, after a hard struggle with neighbouring [Budućnost](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Game between [FK Berane](/wiki/FK_Berane "FK Berane") and FK Budućnost was not even finished, after the crowd disturbances during the second half.[[5]](#cite_note-5) A third derby between Budućnost and Zeta in [Podgorica](/wiki/Podgorica_City_Stadium "Podgorica City Stadium") was attended by 10,000 spectators, which is a record-high attendance in the history of CFL. During the season, many games were disrupted by crowd disturbances[[6]](#cite_note-6) and a match between Zeta and Budućnost in [Golubovci](/wiki/Golubovci "Golubovci") was not played, after the decision was made by the home team not to open their stadium following discussion with [Football Association of Montenegro](/wiki/Football_Association_of_Montenegro "Football Association of Montenegro").[[7]](#cite_note-7)

[Next season](/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_Montenegrin_First_League "2007–08 Montenegrin First League") started with incidents during the [Montenegrin Derby](/wiki/Montenegrin_Derby "Montenegrin Derby") in Nikšić. Budućnost won the title, with the same number of points as Zeta and [Mogren](/wiki/FK_Mogren "FK Mogren"). But, Budućnost had the best score against two opponents from the top of the table. This marked the first trophy for the team from Podgorica.[[8]](#cite_note-8) Their manager at that time [Branko Babić](/wiki/Branko_Babi%C4%87 "Branko Babić") became the first foreign coach to win the Prva CFL title. With an average attendance of *4,250* for their home games, Budućnost made a Montenegrin First League all-time record.

The title winners for [season 2008–09](/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_Montenegrin_First_League "2008–09 Montenegrin First League") became Mogren,[[9]](#cite_note-9) the first-ever club from the coastal Montenegro to win the title. The race for the champions' trophy lasted until the final week, when Mogren won an away game against [Jedinstvo](/wiki/FK_Jedinstvo_Bijelo_Polje "FK Jedinstvo Bijelo Polje") (2-1). At the end of season, they had four points more than second-placed Budućnost and 11 more than the third-place team - Sutjeska.

[A year later](/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Montenegrin_First_League "2009–10 Montenegrin First League") [Rudar](/wiki/FK_Rudar_Pljevlja "FK Rudar Pljevlja")[[10]](#cite_note-10) won the first title in their club's history. They won the trophy after dramatic struggle with Budućnost, and only two points decided the championship race. During that year, [Ivan Bošković](/wiki/Ivan_Bo%C5%A1kovi%C4%87 "Ivan Bošković") from [Grbalj](/wiki/OFK_Grbalj "OFK Grbalj") scored 28 goals, which is the all-time record for one single season. During the last week of season, his team made another record, with the highest victory ever in Montenegrin First League, against [Kom](/wiki/FK_Kom "FK Kom") *(11-0)*.[[11]](#cite_note-auto1-11) During that game, Bošković scored four goals - which is another Prva CFL record, shared with [FK Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta")'s player Miljan Vlaisavljević and [OFK Titograd](/wiki/OFK_Titograd "OFK Titograd")'s player Zoran Petrović.

Mogren became first club to win a second champion trophy in Prva CFL. The team from [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") won the title on season [2010–11](/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Montenegrin_First_League "2010–11 Montenegrin First League"), but with equal number of points as second-placed Budućnost: *(73)*.[[12]](#cite_note-12) In the end, head-to-head scores compared, Mogren were victorious over Budućnost *(2-1; 2-0; 1-2)*.

Budućnost won their second trophy in season [2011–12](/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Montenegrin_First_League "2011–12 Montenegrin First League"),[[13]](#cite_note-13) whilst also setting records for highest number of points in CFL by single season *(80)* and highest number of scored goals by season *(83)*. But, the team from Podgorica didn't win the trophy easily - they were followed by Rudar, who trailed by three points at the end of season. Additionally, Budućnost failed to beat Rudar during the season *(0-2; 2-2; 1-1)*

[Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") became the first club to win two consecutive titles of CFL champion - both times with [Dragan Radojičić](/wiki/Dragan_Radoji%C4%8Di%C4%87 "Dragan Radojičić") as head coach. The team from [Nikšić](/wiki/Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "Nikšić") won the title for seasons [2012–13](/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_Montenegrin_First_League "2012–13 Montenegrin First League") and [2013–14](/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Montenegrin_First_League "2013–14 Montenegrin First League"). Sutjeska headed to their first title with five points more than Budućnost, but secured the trophy on last week of the season.[[14]](#cite_note-14) During that season, Sutjeska for the first time in the First League played city derbies against [Čelik](/wiki/FK_%C4%8Celik_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Čelik Nikšić") *(1-0; 0-3; 0-1)*, who placed third at the end of competition. Second trophy, Sutjeska won after the dramatic spring half-season and struggle with [Lovćen](/wiki/FK_Lov%C4%87en "FK Lovćen"). The title winner was decided a week before the end of season, after a draw between Sutjeska and Lovćen (1-1).[[15]](#cite_note-15) That was the first season on which Budućnost didn't finish in first or second position.

At the end of season [2014–15](/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Montenegrin_First_League "2014–15 Montenegrin First League"), Rudar[[16]](#cite_note-16) won the second title in the club's history. The team from Pljevlja won the race against title holders Sutjeska, who finished second. The team at the bottom of the table - [Berane](/wiki/FK_Berane "FK Berane") at the end of season had only 13 points with 78 goals conceded, which were negative records of Prva CFL at that time. After the [relegation playoffs](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League_playoffs "Montenegrin First League playoffs"), Mogren were relegated to the Second League. This was the first time in history of Prva CFL that former champions were relegated.

The [tenth edition](/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Montenegrin_First_League "2014–15 Montenegrin First League") of Prva CFL finished with a shock, as [OFK Titograd](/wiki/OFK_Titograd "OFK Titograd") from [Podgorica](/wiki/Podgorica "Podgorica") won their first-ever national title.[[17]](#cite_note-17) During this era, OFK Titograd played under the name *Mladost Podgorica*. They won the champions' race against city rivals from Budućnost and during the season, OFK Titograd won all three games against them *(3-1; 1-0; 2-0)*. After the last week, OFK Titograd had four points more than the second-placed team.

In the period from 2006 to 2016, FK Budućnost, FK Sutjeska, FK Rudar and FK Mogren won two champion titles, and FK Zeta and OFK Titograd one. During that time, 19 clubs participated in Prva CFL.

#### 2016–present

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Montenegrin_First_League&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2016–present")]

FK Budućnost won their third champions' title on [season 2016-17](/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Montenegrin_First_League "2016–17 Montenegrin First League"), but with equal number of points as Zeta and OFK Titograd. During the season, six points were deducted from FK Zeta because of irregularities,[[18]](#cite_note-18) so they weren't able to win the trophy. Week before the end of season, on Budućnost - OFK Titograd match, ultras of home team burned a part of north stand at [Podgorica City Stadium](/wiki/Podgorica_City_Stadium "Podgorica City Stadium"), and the game was interrupted and registered with result 0–3.[[19]](#cite_note-19) But, that epilog did not have influence on final placement, as Budućnost finished on the top of the table, with better head-to-head score against OFK Titograd and Zeta.

[Next season](/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_Montenegrin_First_League "2017–18 Montenegrin First League"), FK Sutjeska won their third title.[[20]](#cite_note-20) Team from Nikšić dominated from the very beginning of championship and secured the trophy after 30 weeks. Except that, Sutjeska made a new league record with 11 games without conceded goal. They finished season with 22 points more than second-placed Budućnost.

Season [2018–19](/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Montenegrin_First_League "2018–19 Montenegrin First League") started with the poorest performances of Montenegrin clubs in European competitions since independence. Four teams played 10 games in Champions league and Europa League qualifiers, but without any single win. During the season, FK Sutjeska and FK Budućnost have battle for champions' title and 100th [Montenegrin Derby](/wiki/Montenegrin_Derby "Montenegrin Derby") in [Nikšić](/wiki/Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "Nikšić") was followed by huge incidents after the game, with numerous wounded ultras and policemen.[[21]](#cite_note-21)[[22]](#cite_note-22)[[23]](#cite_note-23)[[24]](#cite_note-24) Week before the end, FK Sutjeska won the title - fourth in team's history. At the same time, [Nikola Rakojević](/wiki/Nikola_Rakojevi%C4%87 "Nikola Rakojević") became the first manager to win three titles. That was the second time in Prva CFL that one club retained the title - both times it did Sutjeska. During the same season, [Mornar](/wiki/FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") finished with 12 points and only one victory from 36 games, which is the all-time negative record in Prva CFL.

Season [2019–20](/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_Montenegrin_First_League "2019–20 Montenegrin First League") started with the title race between FK Budućnost and FK Sutjeska, but the championship was interrupted in March 2020, after 23 weeks, due to the [coronavirus pandemic](/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Montenegro "COVID-19 pandemic in Montenegro"). At that time, FK Budućnost was a leader, with 11 points more than FK Sutjeska. Two months after that, Football Association of Montenegro decided that Prva CFL will be continued on 30 May and that the season will last until 28 July.[[25]](#cite_note-25) But, at the beginning of July, due to COVID-19 case among FK Budućnost players, Football Association of Montenegro decided to stop every official competition. Because of that, placement after 31 week was the final one.[[26]](#cite_note-26) Therefore, FK Budućnost became a new champion. The team from Podgorica secured the title before the final interruption, as they have 18 points more than second-placed squad. Except that, [FK Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Sutjeska Nikšić"), [FK Iskra](/wiki/FK_Iskra_Danilovgrad "FK Iskra Danilovgrad") and [FK Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") qualified for European competitions, too. Last-placed [OFK Grbalj](/wiki/OFK_Grbalj "OFK Grbalj") was directly relegated to [Druga CFL](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League") and [FK Kom](/wiki/FK_Kom "FK Kom") after the playoff games against [FK Jezero](/wiki/FK_Jezero "FK Jezero").[[27]](#cite_note-27)

FK Budućnost defended the trophy on [season 2020-21](/wiki/2020%E2%80%9321_Montenegrin_First_League "2020–21 Montenegrin First League") with 28 points more than second-placed FK Sutjeska. For the first time in teams' history, FK Dečić and FK Podgorica participated in European competition. From the other side, OFK Titograd was directly relegated, while FK Iskra and OFK Petrovac survived via playoffs.

After three years, FK Sutjeska won the new title on [season 2021-22](/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Montenegrin_First_League "2021–22 Montenegrin First League"). FK Budućnost, which won previous two editions, finished as runner-up. Except them, FK Dečić and FK Iskra qualified for European competitions. Big battle for avoiding the relegation lasted until the final week and at the end, first champion of Montenegro, FK Zeta, directly went to Druga CFL, while FK Podgorica was relegated after the playoffs.

  + Since 2017–18: 1 automatic plus the 8th and 9th placed team in the First League plays a [relegation matches](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League_playoffs "Montenegrin First League playoffs") against the second and third placed team of the Second League.

### Rivalries

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Montenegrin_First_League&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Rivalries")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/Varvari-radza.jpg/250px-Varvari-radza.jpg)](/wiki/File:Varvari-radza.jpg)

[FK Budućnost](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica") supporters at [Montenegrin Derby](/wiki/Montenegrin_Derby "Montenegrin Derby") game



Main article: [Montenegrin Derby](/wiki/Montenegrin_Derby "Montenegrin Derby")

The main rivalry in the Montenegrin First League is between [Budućnost](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica") and [Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Sutjeska Nikšić"), often called the [Montenegrin Derby](/wiki/Montenegrin_Derby "Montenegrin Derby"). The first edition of the derby in official competitions was played at 1932,[[28]](#cite_note-28) and the two clubs have played derbies in the highest-tier competitions of SFR Yugoslavia, FR Yugoslavia and in the Montenegrin First League.

Another traditional rivalry is between FK Budućnost and [FK Lovćen Cetinje](/wiki/FK_Lov%C4%87en "FK Lovćen"), because the two clubs have played important games since the 1920s. That rivalry is further fuelled by the fact that Budućnost is the major club from the capital Podgorica, while Lovćen is the main club from the former royal capital, Cetinje.

During the first two seasons of Montenegrin First League, there was a strong rivalry between [Budućnost](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica") and [Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta"). The two clubs from the territory of the [Capital Podgorica](/wiki/Podgorica "Podgorica") were the main candidates for the title during the 2006-07 and 2007–08 seasons, and their match from the spring 2007 was attended by more than 10,000 spectators at Podgorica City Stadium. That is the highest attendance in the history of Montenegrin First League.

During the seasons of 2012-13 and 2013–14, there was a big local derby in [Nikšić](/wiki/Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "Nikšić"), between [Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") and [Čelik](/wiki/FK_%C4%8Celik_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Čelik Nikšić"). At that time, their matches were often attended by more than 7,000 supporters.

In the new period, there was a strong title races between [Rudar](/wiki/FK_Rudar_Pljevlja "FK Rudar Pljevlja") and [Budućnost](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica") or [Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") and [Rudar](/wiki/FK_Rudar_Pljevlja "FK Rudar Pljevlja").

### Relegation and promotion

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Montenegrin_First_League&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Relegation and promotion")]

At the end of every season, the last placed team are relegated to the [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League"), while the winner of Second League is promoted to highest-rank. Additionally, another two teams from First and Second League every season are participating in the playoffs.

### History

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Montenegrin_First_League&action=edit&section=35 "Edit section: History")]

Main article: [Montenegrin clubs in European football competitions](/wiki/Montenegrin_clubs_in_European_football_competitions "Montenegrin clubs in European football competitions")

Montenegrin football clubs have played in four [UEFA](/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") competitions - the [UEFA Champions League](/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League"), [UEFA Europa League](/wiki/UEFA_Europa_League "UEFA Europa League") (*formerly UEFA Cup*) and [Intertoto Cup](/wiki/Intertoto_Cup "Intertoto Cup").  
Champions of Montenegro have never played in the group-phase of UEFA Champions League, and the most successful in the qualifiers was [FK Zeta Golubovci](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") in the 2007–08 season and [FK Sutjeska Nikšić](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") in 2019–20.  
FK Zeta had the best performances in the UEFA Europa League: reaching the playoffs, and [OFK Titograd](/wiki/OFK_Titograd "OFK Titograd"), FK Budućnost and FK Sutjeska which played in Round 3.   
[FK Mornar](/wiki/FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") and [FK Dečić](/wiki/FK_De%C4%8Di%C4%87 "FK Dečić") had the best performances in the UEFA Conference League: reaching the Round 3.  
The most successful in the Intertoto Cup was [Budućnost](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"), which was among the winners during the 1981 season.

Logo and sponsorships
---------------------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Montenegrin_First_League&action=edit&section=37 "Edit section: Logo and sponsorships")]

### Official logo and equipment

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Montenegrin_First_League&action=edit&section=38 "Edit section: Official logo and equipment")]

Since establishment, the Montenegrin First League has had two official logos.

The first logo was presented in 2006. Rebranding of the league came in 2018, together with the new logos of the [Montenegrin Cup](/wiki/Montenegrin_Cup "Montenegrin Cup"), [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League") and youth leagues.[[55]](#cite_note-55)

The official ball of the competition is produced under the *Derbystar* brand, while the official equipment of referees is a product of [Legea](/wiki/Legea "Legea").

### Sponsorships

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Montenegrin_First_League&action=edit&section=39 "Edit section: Sponsorships")]

#### Name of the competition

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Montenegrin_First_League&action=edit&section=40 "Edit section: Name of the competition")]

Since foundation, the main sponsor of Montenegrin First League has been Montenegrin 'Telekom' which operates under the T-Com / T-Mobile brand. Since July 2022, the main sponsor of the First Montenegrin Football League is Meridianbet company.

* 2006–2011: **[T-Com](/wiki/T-Mobile_International_AG "T-Mobile International AG") 1. CFL**
* 2011–2022: **[Telekom](/wiki/T-Mobile_International_AG "T-Mobile International AG") 1. CFL**
* 2022–present: **[Meridianbet](https://meridianbet.me/) 1. CFL**

#### Broadcasting rights

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Montenegrin_First_League&action=edit&section=41 "Edit section: Broadcasting rights")]

Since the foundation of the competition, official broadcaster of First Montenegrin League matches is [RTCG](/wiki/RTCG "RTCG"), the national television station of Montenegro. Matches of 1. CFL are directly broadcast on [TVCG 2](/wiki/TVCG_2 "TVCG 2"), with most important matches on the satellite channel.

From season 2017–18, broadcaster of matches is regional group [Arena Sport](/wiki/Arena_Sport "Arena Sport"). Every weekend, one game is broadcast live on Arena Sport channel.[[56]](#cite_note-56) Since season 2018–19, some games of Prva CFL are broadcast by cable-network channel *MNE Sport TV*.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

**Žarko Korać** ([Cyrillic](/wiki/Cyrillic "Cyrillic"): Жapкo Kopaћ, born 11 June 1987) is a [Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegrins_(ethnic_group) "Montenegrins (ethnic group)") [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") player who plays as a [forward](/wiki/Forward_(association_football) "Forward (association football)") for [FK Jedinstvo](/wiki/FK_Jedinstvo_Bijelo_Polje "FK Jedinstvo Bijelo Polje").

Club career
-----------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C5%BDarko_Kora%C4%87_(footballer)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Club career")]

Žarko has played mainly with Montenegrin club [FK Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta"), having achieved the title of Montenegrin First League top scorer in the season 2006–07.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

After this early success, he decided to move abroad signing a contract with [Serbian SuperLiga](/wiki/Serbian_SuperLiga "Serbian SuperLiga") club [FK Vojvodina](/wiki/FK_Vojvodina "FK Vojvodina"). After not getting many chances there, he returned to [FK Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") in December 2008. He played there until January 2010 when he moved to Moldovan club [FC Sheriff Tiraspol](/wiki/FC_Sheriff_Tiraspol "FC Sheriff Tiraspol").[[2]](#cite_note-2)
In summer 2010 he returned to Zeta where he became a regular at the starting 11.

He finished the [2012–13 Montenegrin First League](/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_Montenegrin_First_League "2012–13 Montenegrin First League") season as the co-top scorer with 15 goals.
following this success he has been loaned to [Hapoel Haifa](/wiki/Hapoel_Haifa_F.C. "Hapoel Haifa F.C.") of the [Israeli Premier League](/wiki/Israeli_Premier_League "Israeli Premier League"), where he scored 11 goals, finishing as the 5th top scorer in the league.

on June 2, 2014, Korać has signed a 4-years contract with Israeli club [Beitar Jerusalem](/wiki/Beitar_Jerusalem_F.C. "Beitar Jerusalem F.C."), with a salary of €160,000 per season. Beitar also paid €160,000 to Hapoel Haifa for his service.[[3]](#cite_note-3) After just half a season in Beitar, Korać returned to Hapoel Haifa, where he played for two seasons between 2015 and 2017.

**Žarko Korać** ([Cyrillic](/wiki/Cyrillic "Cyrillic"): Жapкo Kopaћ, born 11 June 1987) is a [Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegrins_(ethnic_group) "Montenegrins (ethnic group)") [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") player who plays as a [forward](/wiki/Forward_(association_football) "Forward (association football)") for [FK Jedinstvo](/wiki/FK_Jedinstvo_Bijelo_Polje "FK Jedinstvo Bijelo Polje").

Club career
-----------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C5%BDarko_Kora%C4%87_(footballer)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Club career")]

Žarko has played mainly with Montenegrin club [FK Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta"), having achieved the title of Montenegrin First League top scorer in the season 2006–07.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

After this early success, he decided to move abroad signing a contract with [Serbian SuperLiga](/wiki/Serbian_SuperLiga "Serbian SuperLiga") club [FK Vojvodina](/wiki/FK_Vojvodina "FK Vojvodina"). After not getting many chances there, he returned to [FK Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") in December 2008. He played there until January 2010 when he moved to Moldovan club [FC Sheriff Tiraspol](/wiki/FC_Sheriff_Tiraspol "FC Sheriff Tiraspol").[[2]](#cite_note-2)
In summer 2010 he returned to Zeta where he became a regular at the starting 11.

He finished the [2012–13 Montenegrin First League](/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_Montenegrin_First_League "2012–13 Montenegrin First League") season as the co-top scorer with 15 goals.
following this success he has been loaned to [Hapoel Haifa](/wiki/Hapoel_Haifa_F.C. "Hapoel Haifa F.C.") of the [Israeli Premier League](/wiki/Israeli_Premier_League "Israeli Premier League"), where he scored 11 goals, finishing as the 5th top scorer in the league.

on June 2, 2014, Korać has signed a 4-years contract with Israeli club [Beitar Jerusalem](/wiki/Beitar_Jerusalem_F.C. "Beitar Jerusalem F.C."), with a salary of €160,000 per season. Beitar also paid €160,000 to Hapoel Haifa for his service.[[3]](#cite_note-3) After just half a season in Beitar, Korać returned to Hapoel Haifa, where he played for two seasons between 2015 and 2017.

**Fudbalski klub Jedinstvo** ([Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegrin_language "Montenegrin language"): Фудбалски клуб Јединство), known as **Jedinstvo Franca** for sponsorship reasons, is [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") club from [Bijelo Polje](/wiki/Bijelo_Polje "Bijelo Polje"), [Montenegro](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro"), currently competing in the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). The club was established in 1922.

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=FK_Jedinstvo_Bijelo_Polje&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

FK Jedinstvo (*FC United*) was founded in 1922, as a first football team in [Bijelo Polje](/wiki/Bijelo_Polje "Bijelo Polje"). During the first two decades (1922–1941), the team played mostly exhibition matches, without participation in [Montenegrin Football Championship](/wiki/Montenegrin_Football_Championship_(1922%E2%80%931940) "Montenegrin Football Championship (1922–1940)").

First significant success after [World War II](/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), the team made on season 1949–50, with promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](/wiki/Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946%E2%80%932006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)").[[1]](#cite_note-1) At that time, the club played under the name *Bratstvo*. Soon after that, in the 1955–56 season, FK Jedinstvo played their first-ever season in the [Yugoslav Second League](/wiki/Yugoslav_Second_League "Yugoslav Second League"), but were relegated after three consecutive seasons.

Most of the sixties, FK Jedinstvo spent in Republic League, until the 1967–68 season. On that year, the team finished third place and gained promotion to the [Yugoslav Second League – South Group](/wiki/Yugoslav_Second_League "Yugoslav Second League"). After two seasons, they were relegated, but new promotion to second-tier came in 1971, when FK Jedinstvo won the title of the Montenegrin Republic League champion. New season in the Second League, FK Jedinstvo finished as a last-placed team in *South* group. In the period between 1975 and 1980, FK Jedinstvo won two titles in the Republic League.

Difficult times came at the beginning of the 1980s. On Republic League 1980–81 season, FK Jedinstvo finished 12th place, so, for the first time in their history, the team were relegated to the lowest-rank of domestic football system ([Fourth League – North](/wiki/Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946%E2%80%932006)#Montenegrin_regional_league_system "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)").[[2]](#cite_note-2)). They made comeback in the 1982–83 season. In that season, FK Jedinstvo played in the [Yugoslav Cup](/wiki/1982%E2%80%9383_Yugoslav_Cup "1982–83 Yugoslav Cup"). In the First Round, they hosted one of the most successful teams in the history of Yugoslav football – [Dinamo Zagreb](/wiki/GNK_Dinamo_Zagreb "GNK Dinamo Zagreb") in front of 6,000 spectators (0–2). Two years later, FK Jedinstvo were faced with another relegation to the Fourth League. At that time, in Bijelo Polje, they were in the shadow of local-rival [FK Tekstilac](/wiki/FK_Tekstilac "FK Tekstilac").  
In the 1988–89 season, FK Jedinstvo played in newly established [Yugoslav Inter-Republic League](/wiki/Yugoslav_Inter-Republic_League "Yugoslav Inter-Republic League") (third division), where they made significant success in the 1990–91 season. As a second-placed team, the team gained promotion to the [1991–92 Yugoslav Second League](/wiki/1991%E2%80%9392_Yugoslav_Second_League "1991–92 Yugoslav Second League"). On their comeback to second-tier, FK Jedinstvo finished 14th place.[[3]](#cite_note-3)

After the breakup of [SFR Yugoslavia](/wiki/SFR_Yugoslavia "SFR Yugoslavia"), FK Jedinstvo spent most of the nineties in the second-tier competitions of [FR Yugoslavia](/wiki/FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia"). In the beginning of the new century, the team from Bijelo Polje were among the best teams in the [Second League of Serbia and Montenegro](/wiki/Second_League_of_Serbia_and_Montenegro "Second League of Serbia and Montenegro").

Historical success came in the 2004–05 season. FK Jedinstvo won the champion title in [Second League – group Montenegro](/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_Montenegrin_First_League "2004–05 Montenegrin First League") and gained its first-ever promotion to the [First League of Serbia and Montenegro](/wiki/First_League_of_Serbia_and_Montenegro "First League of Serbia and Montenegro").[[4]](#cite_note-4)  
They started the [2005–06 Serbia and Montenegro SuperLiga](/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_Serbia_and_Montenegro_SuperLiga "2005–06 Serbia and Montenegro SuperLiga") season with the game against [FK Partizan](/wiki/FK_Partizan "FK Partizan") away (0–2), and first-ever elite division game in Bijelo Polje was held on 27 August 2005 (FK Jedinstvo – [FK Voždovac](/wiki/FK_Vo%C5%BEdovac "FK Voždovac") 2–2).[[5]](#cite_note-5) FK Jedinstvo finished at the bottom of table, but their home games were among the best attended in the First League.
After the [Montenegrin independence](/wiki/Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006") (2006), FK Jedinstvo became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"), but relegated to the [Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League") after the inaugural season.[[6]](#cite_note-6) In the period between 2008 and 2018, FK Jedinstvo spent three another years in the First League, but were always relegated at the end of the season as a last-placed team.

Stadium
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=FK_Jedinstvo_Bijelo_Polje&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Stadium")]

Main article: [Gradski stadion (Bijelo Polje)](/wiki/Gradski_stadion_(Bijelo_Polje) "Gradski stadion (Bijelo Polje)")

FK Jedinstvo plays their home games on [Gradski stadion](/wiki/Gradski_stadion_(Bijelo_Polje) "Gradski stadion (Bijelo Polje)"). There are two stands with overall capacity of 4,000 seats. At the north side of stadium is situated indoor sports hall 'Nikoljac'.

**Omladinski fudbalski klub Grbalj** ([Serbian Cyrillic](/wiki/Serbian_Cyrillic_alphabet "Serbian Cyrillic alphabet"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")) is a [Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](/wiki/Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor "Radanovići, Kotor"), municipality of [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](/wiki/Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946%E2%80%932006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](/wiki/FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](/wiki/1999%E2%80%932000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia "1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  
After [Montenegrin independence](/wiki/Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") and [Budućnost Podgorica](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn't achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  
OFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](/wiki/FK_Kom "FK Kom") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](/wiki/FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") in [Bar](/wiki/Bar,_Montenegro "Bar, Montenegro") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  
In the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Montenegrin_Cup "2016–17 Montenegrin Cup"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") 1–0.  
After 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](/wiki/2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League "2019-20 Montenegrin First League"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League").

Stadium
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Stadium")]

Main article: [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara")

OFK Grbalj play at [Stadion Donja Sutvara](/wiki/Stadion_Donja_Sutvara "Stadion Donja Sutvara"), near the main road between [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") and [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor "Kotor"). Stadium capacity is 1,500 seats on one stand and it doesn't meet UEFA standards for European competitions. Except the main ground, there is a smaller artificial pitch at Donja Sutvara football complex.

The **Montenegrin First League** ([Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegrin_language "Montenegrin language"): *Prva crnogorska fudbalska liga* — *Prva CFL* — *1. CFL*; pronounced [[pr̂ːvaː t͡srnǒɡorskaː fûdbaːlskaː lǐːɡa]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian "Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian")), referred to as the **Meridianbet 1. CFL** for sponsorship reasons,[[1]](#cite_note-1) is the top professional [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") league in Montenegro. Founded in 2006, the competition is headed by the [Football Association of Montenegro](/wiki/Football_Association_of_Montenegro "Football Association of Montenegro"). 10 teams participate in this league. The winner of the Montenegrin First League enter the qualifications for the [UEFA Champions League](/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League") from the first round. The second and third placed teams and [Montenegrin Cup](/wiki/Montenegrin_Cup "Montenegrin Cup") winner play in the qualifying rounds of the [UEFA Conference League](/wiki/UEFA_Conference_League "UEFA Conference League"). The last placed team is directly [relegated](/wiki/Promotion_and_relegation "Promotion and relegation") to the [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League"), and the two next lowest ranked teams play in [Montenegrin First League playoffs](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League_playoffs "Montenegrin First League playoffs").

As a part of the [Kingdom of Yugoslavia](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Yugoslavia "Kingdom of Yugoslavia"), Montenegrin clubs played in the [Montenegrin Football Championship](/wiki/Montenegrin_Football_Championship_(1922%E2%80%931940) "Montenegrin Football Championship (1922–1940)") which was formed in 1922.[[2]](#cite_note-vijesti1-2)[[3]](#cite_note-3)[[4]](#cite_note-4) Despite the presence of the nationwide [Yugoslav Football Championship](/wiki/Yugoslav_Football_Championship "Yugoslav Football Championship"), Montenegrin teams did not partake in it. Montenegrin Football Championship played until the beginning of World War II.

The most successful teams at that period were *SK Crnogorac Cetinje* (10 titles), *GSK Balšić Podgorica* (7), [FK Lovćen Cetinje](/wiki/FK_Lov%C4%87en_Cetinje "FK Lovćen Cetinje") (5), [FK Budućnost Podgorica](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica") (4) and [FK Arsenal Tivat](/wiki/FK_Arsenal_Tivat "FK Arsenal Tivat") (1). While SK Crnogorac and GSK Balšić played all the seasons, work of FK Budućnost and FK Lovćen was forbidden in 1935, as they were recognized as workers' clubs by [Kingdom of Yugoslavia](/wiki/Kingdom_of_Yugoslavia "Kingdom of Yugoslavia") government and forbidden.

After [World War II](/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") and the formation of the [Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia](/wiki/Socialist_Federal_Republic_of_Yugoslavia "Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia"), the top league became the [Yugoslav First League](/wiki/Yugoslav_First_League "Yugoslav First League"). Montenegrin teams were allowed to partake in the nationwide league structure, with a [Montenegrin Republic League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin Republic League") acting as a lower-tier division with promotion and relegation between the Yugoslav league system. The most prominent clubs from Montenegro in this period were [FK Budućnost](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica") and [FK Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Sutjeska Nikšić").

FK Budućnost was among the founders of [Yugoslav First League](/wiki/Yugoslav_First_League "Yugoslav First League") and a member of its inaugural season. During the most of SFRY era, FK Budućnost played in First League, while another team from Montenegro in top-tier was FK Sutjeska. Other teams played in [Yugoslav Second League](/wiki/Yugoslav_Second_League "Yugoslav Second League") or lower ranks. Among them, most successful was FK Lovćen, who played twice in First League qualifiers, but without success at the end of campaigns.

In 1992 when SFR Yugoslavia dissolved the [Federal Republic of Yugoslavia](/wiki/Federal_Republic_of_Yugoslavia "Federal Republic of Yugoslavia") was formed. Serbian and Montenegrin teams played in its national league, although it was still named *Yugoslav First League*. In 2003, FR Yugoslavia became [Serbia and Montenegro](/wiki/Serbia_and_Montenegro "Serbia and Montenegro") and the football league was renamed. Montenegrin clubs played in the First League with Serbian clubs from 1992 to 2006. In that period, representatives of Montenegro in the Yugoslav/Serbia and Montenegro First League were FK Budućnost, FK Sutjeska, [FK Rudar](/wiki/FK_Rudar_Pljevlja "FK Rudar Pljevlja"), [FK Mogren](/wiki/FK_Mogren "FK Mogren"), [FK Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta"), [FK Kom](/wiki/FK_Kom "FK Kom") and [FK Jedinstvo](/wiki/FK_Jedinstvo_Bijelo_Polje "FK Jedinstvo Bijelo Polje").

For 2004–05, restructuring of the Serbo-Montenegrin football league system saw the dissolution of the [national second league](/wiki/Second_League_of_Serbia_and_Montenegro "Second League of Serbia and Montenegro"), instead being replaced by two regional divisions for both republics of the union with promotion to the still-united First League.

Montenegrin teams which played in European competitions during Yugoslav era were FK Budućnost, FK Sutjeska and FK Zeta.

### After independence

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Montenegrin_First_League&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: After independence")]

In 2006, after the [Independence referendum](/wiki/Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006"), Montenegro split from Serbia. Following that, Montenegrin First League is founded as top-tier national competition. On inaugural season, members of League became three teams from former First League of Serbia and Montenegro, seven from Second League, and two from [Montenegrin Republic League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin Republic League").

Between 2006 and 2017, the league consisted on 12 clubs, which played 33 matches during the season. From the [2017-18 season](/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_Montenegrin_First_League "2017–18 Montenegrin First League") the number of participants in the Montenegrin First League was reduced to 10, with a 36 week-long competition.

20 clubs have participated in the Montenegrin First League. The most successful are FK Sutjeska with five titles and FK Budućnost five national titles too. FK Rudar and FK Mogren won two titles. Other winners were FK Zeta and OFK Titograd with one title.

#### 2006–16

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Montenegrin_First_League&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2006–16")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/0/0e/T-com_Prva_CFL.gif)](/wiki/File:T-com_Prva_CFL.gif)

Official logo 2007–2018

The first game in Prva CFL was played on 11 August 2006 in [Pljevlja](/wiki/Pljevlja "Pljevlja"). In front of 5,000 spectators, a game between the home side [FK Rudar](/wiki/FK_Rudar_Pljevlja "FK Rudar Pljevlja") and [FK Budućnost](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"), finished with a victory of the away team (0-2). In the fifth minute of that match, [Ivan Čarapić](/w/index.php?title=Ivan_%C4%8Carapi%C4%87&action=edit&redlink=1 "Ivan Čarapić (page does not exist)") (Budućnost) scored the first goal in the history of Prva CFL.

The [first champion](/wiki/2006%E2%80%9307_Montenegrin_First_League "2006–07 Montenegrin First League") of the top-tier CFL was [Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta"), who won the trophy on the championship's final weekend, after a hard struggle with neighbouring [Budućnost](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"). Game between [FK Berane](/wiki/FK_Berane "FK Berane") and FK Budućnost was not even finished, after the crowd disturbances during the second half.[[5]](#cite_note-5) A third derby between Budućnost and Zeta in [Podgorica](/wiki/Podgorica_City_Stadium "Podgorica City Stadium") was attended by 10,000 spectators, which is a record-high attendance in the history of CFL. During the season, many games were disrupted by crowd disturbances[[6]](#cite_note-6) and a match between Zeta and Budućnost in [Golubovci](/wiki/Golubovci "Golubovci") was not played, after the decision was made by the home team not to open their stadium following discussion with [Football Association of Montenegro](/wiki/Football_Association_of_Montenegro "Football Association of Montenegro").[[7]](#cite_note-7)

[Next season](/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_Montenegrin_First_League "2007–08 Montenegrin First League") started with incidents during the [Montenegrin Derby](/wiki/Montenegrin_Derby "Montenegrin Derby") in Nikšić. Budućnost won the title, with the same number of points as Zeta and [Mogren](/wiki/FK_Mogren "FK Mogren"). But, Budućnost had the best score against two opponents from the top of the table. This marked the first trophy for the team from Podgorica.[[8]](#cite_note-8) Their manager at that time [Branko Babić](/wiki/Branko_Babi%C4%87 "Branko Babić") became the first foreign coach to win the Prva CFL title. With an average attendance of *4,250* for their home games, Budućnost made a Montenegrin First League all-time record.

The title winners for [season 2008–09](/wiki/2008%E2%80%9309_Montenegrin_First_League "2008–09 Montenegrin First League") became Mogren,[[9]](#cite_note-9) the first-ever club from the coastal Montenegro to win the title. The race for the champions' trophy lasted until the final week, when Mogren won an away game against [Jedinstvo](/wiki/FK_Jedinstvo_Bijelo_Polje "FK Jedinstvo Bijelo Polje") (2-1). At the end of season, they had four points more than second-placed Budućnost and 11 more than the third-place team - Sutjeska.

[A year later](/wiki/2009%E2%80%9310_Montenegrin_First_League "2009–10 Montenegrin First League") [Rudar](/wiki/FK_Rudar_Pljevlja "FK Rudar Pljevlja")[[10]](#cite_note-10) won the first title in their club's history. They won the trophy after dramatic struggle with Budućnost, and only two points decided the championship race. During that year, [Ivan Bošković](/wiki/Ivan_Bo%C5%A1kovi%C4%87 "Ivan Bošković") from [Grbalj](/wiki/OFK_Grbalj "OFK Grbalj") scored 28 goals, which is the all-time record for one single season. During the last week of season, his team made another record, with the highest victory ever in Montenegrin First League, against [Kom](/wiki/FK_Kom "FK Kom") *(11-0)*.[[11]](#cite_note-auto1-11) During that game, Bošković scored four goals - which is another Prva CFL record, shared with [FK Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta")'s player Miljan Vlaisavljević and [OFK Titograd](/wiki/OFK_Titograd "OFK Titograd")'s player Zoran Petrović.

Mogren became first club to win a second champion trophy in Prva CFL. The team from [Budva](/wiki/Budva "Budva") won the title on season [2010–11](/wiki/2010%E2%80%9311_Montenegrin_First_League "2010–11 Montenegrin First League"), but with equal number of points as second-placed Budućnost: *(73)*.[[12]](#cite_note-12) In the end, head-to-head scores compared, Mogren were victorious over Budućnost *(2-1; 2-0; 1-2)*.

Budućnost won their second trophy in season [2011–12](/wiki/2011%E2%80%9312_Montenegrin_First_League "2011–12 Montenegrin First League"),[[13]](#cite_note-13) whilst also setting records for highest number of points in CFL by single season *(80)* and highest number of scored goals by season *(83)*. But, the team from Podgorica didn't win the trophy easily - they were followed by Rudar, who trailed by three points at the end of season. Additionally, Budućnost failed to beat Rudar during the season *(0-2; 2-2; 1-1)*

[Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") became the first club to win two consecutive titles of CFL champion - both times with [Dragan Radojičić](/wiki/Dragan_Radoji%C4%8Di%C4%87 "Dragan Radojičić") as head coach. The team from [Nikšić](/wiki/Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "Nikšić") won the title for seasons [2012–13](/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_Montenegrin_First_League "2012–13 Montenegrin First League") and [2013–14](/wiki/2013%E2%80%9314_Montenegrin_First_League "2013–14 Montenegrin First League"). Sutjeska headed to their first title with five points more than Budućnost, but secured the trophy on last week of the season.[[14]](#cite_note-14) During that season, Sutjeska for the first time in the First League played city derbies against [Čelik](/wiki/FK_%C4%8Celik_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Čelik Nikšić") *(1-0; 0-3; 0-1)*, who placed third at the end of competition. Second trophy, Sutjeska won after the dramatic spring half-season and struggle with [Lovćen](/wiki/FK_Lov%C4%87en "FK Lovćen"). The title winner was decided a week before the end of season, after a draw between Sutjeska and Lovćen (1-1).[[15]](#cite_note-15) That was the first season on which Budućnost didn't finish in first or second position.

At the end of season [2014–15](/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Montenegrin_First_League "2014–15 Montenegrin First League"), Rudar[[16]](#cite_note-16) won the second title in the club's history. The team from Pljevlja won the race against title holders Sutjeska, who finished second. The team at the bottom of the table - [Berane](/wiki/FK_Berane "FK Berane") at the end of season had only 13 points with 78 goals conceded, which were negative records of Prva CFL at that time. After the [relegation playoffs](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League_playoffs "Montenegrin First League playoffs"), Mogren were relegated to the Second League. This was the first time in history of Prva CFL that former champions were relegated.

The [tenth edition](/wiki/2014%E2%80%9315_Montenegrin_First_League "2014–15 Montenegrin First League") of Prva CFL finished with a shock, as [OFK Titograd](/wiki/OFK_Titograd "OFK Titograd") from [Podgorica](/wiki/Podgorica "Podgorica") won their first-ever national title.[[17]](#cite_note-17) During this era, OFK Titograd played under the name *Mladost Podgorica*. They won the champions' race against city rivals from Budućnost and during the season, OFK Titograd won all three games against them *(3-1; 1-0; 2-0)*. After the last week, OFK Titograd had four points more than the second-placed team.

In the period from 2006 to 2016, FK Budućnost, FK Sutjeska, FK Rudar and FK Mogren won two champion titles, and FK Zeta and OFK Titograd one. During that time, 19 clubs participated in Prva CFL.

#### 2016–present

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Montenegrin_First_League&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2016–present")]

FK Budućnost won their third champions' title on [season 2016-17](/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Montenegrin_First_League "2016–17 Montenegrin First League"), but with equal number of points as Zeta and OFK Titograd. During the season, six points were deducted from FK Zeta because of irregularities,[[18]](#cite_note-18) so they weren't able to win the trophy. Week before the end of season, on Budućnost - OFK Titograd match, ultras of home team burned a part of north stand at [Podgorica City Stadium](/wiki/Podgorica_City_Stadium "Podgorica City Stadium"), and the game was interrupted and registered with result 0–3.[[19]](#cite_note-19) But, that epilog did not have influence on final placement, as Budućnost finished on the top of the table, with better head-to-head score against OFK Titograd and Zeta.

[Next season](/wiki/2017%E2%80%9318_Montenegrin_First_League "2017–18 Montenegrin First League"), FK Sutjeska won their third title.[[20]](#cite_note-20) Team from Nikšić dominated from the very beginning of championship and secured the trophy after 30 weeks. Except that, Sutjeska made a new league record with 11 games without conceded goal. They finished season with 22 points more than second-placed Budućnost.

Season [2018–19](/wiki/2018%E2%80%9319_Montenegrin_First_League "2018–19 Montenegrin First League") started with the poorest performances of Montenegrin clubs in European competitions since independence. Four teams played 10 games in Champions league and Europa League qualifiers, but without any single win. During the season, FK Sutjeska and FK Budućnost have battle for champions' title and 100th [Montenegrin Derby](/wiki/Montenegrin_Derby "Montenegrin Derby") in [Nikšić](/wiki/Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "Nikšić") was followed by huge incidents after the game, with numerous wounded ultras and policemen.[[21]](#cite_note-21)[[22]](#cite_note-22)[[23]](#cite_note-23)[[24]](#cite_note-24) Week before the end, FK Sutjeska won the title - fourth in team's history. At the same time, [Nikola Rakojević](/wiki/Nikola_Rakojevi%C4%87 "Nikola Rakojević") became the first manager to win three titles. That was the second time in Prva CFL that one club retained the title - both times it did Sutjeska. During the same season, [Mornar](/wiki/FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") finished with 12 points and only one victory from 36 games, which is the all-time negative record in Prva CFL.

Season [2019–20](/wiki/2019%E2%80%9320_Montenegrin_First_League "2019–20 Montenegrin First League") started with the title race between FK Budućnost and FK Sutjeska, but the championship was interrupted in March 2020, after 23 weeks, due to the [coronavirus pandemic](/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Montenegro "COVID-19 pandemic in Montenegro"). At that time, FK Budućnost was a leader, with 11 points more than FK Sutjeska. Two months after that, Football Association of Montenegro decided that Prva CFL will be continued on 30 May and that the season will last until 28 July.[[25]](#cite_note-25) But, at the beginning of July, due to COVID-19 case among FK Budućnost players, Football Association of Montenegro decided to stop every official competition. Because of that, placement after 31 week was the final one.[[26]](#cite_note-26) Therefore, FK Budućnost became a new champion. The team from Podgorica secured the title before the final interruption, as they have 18 points more than second-placed squad. Except that, [FK Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Sutjeska Nikšić"), [FK Iskra](/wiki/FK_Iskra_Danilovgrad "FK Iskra Danilovgrad") and [FK Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") qualified for European competitions, too. Last-placed [OFK Grbalj](/wiki/OFK_Grbalj "OFK Grbalj") was directly relegated to [Druga CFL](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League") and [FK Kom](/wiki/FK_Kom "FK Kom") after the playoff games against [FK Jezero](/wiki/FK_Jezero "FK Jezero").[[27]](#cite_note-27)

FK Budućnost defended the trophy on [season 2020-21](/wiki/2020%E2%80%9321_Montenegrin_First_League "2020–21 Montenegrin First League") with 28 points more than second-placed FK Sutjeska. For the first time in teams' history, FK Dečić and FK Podgorica participated in European competition. From the other side, OFK Titograd was directly relegated, while FK Iskra and OFK Petrovac survived via playoffs.

After three years, FK Sutjeska won the new title on [season 2021-22](/wiki/2021%E2%80%9322_Montenegrin_First_League "2021–22 Montenegrin First League"). FK Budućnost, which won previous two editions, finished as runner-up. Except them, FK Dečić and FK Iskra qualified for European competitions. Big battle for avoiding the relegation lasted until the final week and at the end, first champion of Montenegro, FK Zeta, directly went to Druga CFL, while FK Podgorica was relegated after the playoffs.

### Changes in league structure

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Montenegrin_First_League&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Changes in league structure")]

* Number of teams:
  + 2006–07 to 2016–17: **12**
  + Since 2017–18: **10**
* Number of teams relegated:
  + 2006–07 to 2016–17: 1 automatic plus the 10th and 11th placed team in the First League played a two-leg [relegation matches](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League_playoffs "Montenegrin First League playoffs") against the second and third placed team of the Second League.
  + Since 2017–18: 1 automatic plus the 8th and 9th placed team in the First League plays a [relegation matches](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League_playoffs "Montenegrin First League playoffs") against the second and third placed team of the Second League.

### Rivalries

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Montenegrin_First_League&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Rivalries")]

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/Varvari-radza.jpg/250px-Varvari-radza.jpg)](/wiki/File:Varvari-radza.jpg)

[FK Budućnost](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica") supporters at [Montenegrin Derby](/wiki/Montenegrin_Derby "Montenegrin Derby") game



Main article: [Montenegrin Derby](/wiki/Montenegrin_Derby "Montenegrin Derby")

The main rivalry in the Montenegrin First League is between [Budućnost](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica") and [Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Sutjeska Nikšić"), often called the [Montenegrin Derby](/wiki/Montenegrin_Derby "Montenegrin Derby"). The first edition of the derby in official competitions was played at 1932,[[28]](#cite_note-28) and the two clubs have played derbies in the highest-tier competitions of SFR Yugoslavia, FR Yugoslavia and in the Montenegrin First League.

Another traditional rivalry is between FK Budućnost and [FK Lovćen Cetinje](/wiki/FK_Lov%C4%87en "FK Lovćen"), because the two clubs have played important games since the 1920s. That rivalry is further fuelled by the fact that Budućnost is the major club from the capital Podgorica, while Lovćen is the main club from the former royal capital, Cetinje.

During the first two seasons of Montenegrin First League, there was a strong rivalry between [Budućnost](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica") and [Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta"). The two clubs from the territory of the [Capital Podgorica](/wiki/Podgorica "Podgorica") were the main candidates for the title during the 2006-07 and 2007–08 seasons, and their match from the spring 2007 was attended by more than 10,000 spectators at Podgorica City Stadium. That is the highest attendance in the history of Montenegrin First League.

During the seasons of 2012-13 and 2013–14, there was a big local derby in [Nikšić](/wiki/Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "Nikšić"), between [Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") and [Čelik](/wiki/FK_%C4%8Celik_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Čelik Nikšić"). At that time, their matches were often attended by more than 7,000 supporters.

In the new period, there was a strong title races between [Rudar](/wiki/FK_Rudar_Pljevlja "FK Rudar Pljevlja") and [Budućnost](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica") or [Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") and [Rudar](/wiki/FK_Rudar_Pljevlja "FK Rudar Pljevlja").

### Champions

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Montenegrin_First_League&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Champions")]

Since its inception in the [2006–07 season](/wiki/2006%E2%80%9307_Montenegrin_First_League "2006–07 Montenegrin First League"), six clubs have won the title. As of the culmination of the 2020–21 season, [Budućnost](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica") have won 5 titles, followed by [Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") with 4, while [Rudar](/wiki/FK_Rudar_Pljevlja "FK Rudar Pljevlja") and [Mogren](/wiki/FK_Mogren "FK Mogren") each won 2. Only Budućnost and Sutjeska managed to retain their title in the following season; furthermore, Sutjeska managed to do so twice.

### Relegation and promotion

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Montenegrin_First_League&action=edit&section=23 "Edit section: Relegation and promotion")]

At the end of every season, the last placed team are relegated to the [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League"), while the winner of Second League is promoted to highest-rank. Additionally, another two teams from First and Second League every season are participating in the playoffs.

### History

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Montenegrin_First_League&action=edit&section=35 "Edit section: History")]

Main article: [Montenegrin clubs in European football competitions](/wiki/Montenegrin_clubs_in_European_football_competitions "Montenegrin clubs in European football competitions")

Montenegrin football clubs have played in four [UEFA](/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") competitions - the [UEFA Champions League](/wiki/UEFA_Champions_League "UEFA Champions League"), [UEFA Europa League](/wiki/UEFA_Europa_League "UEFA Europa League") (*formerly UEFA Cup*) and [Intertoto Cup](/wiki/Intertoto_Cup "Intertoto Cup").  
Champions of Montenegro have never played in the group-phase of UEFA Champions League, and the most successful in the qualifiers was [FK Zeta Golubovci](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") in the 2007–08 season and [FK Sutjeska Nikšić](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 "FK Sutjeska Nikšić") in 2019–20.  
FK Zeta had the best performances in the UEFA Europa League: reaching the playoffs, and [OFK Titograd](/wiki/OFK_Titograd "OFK Titograd"), FK Budućnost and FK Sutjeska which played in Round 3.   
[FK Mornar](/wiki/FK_Mornar "FK Mornar") and [FK Dečić](/wiki/FK_De%C4%8Di%C4%87 "FK Dečić") had the best performances in the UEFA Conference League: reaching the Round 3.  
The most successful in the Intertoto Cup was [Budućnost](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica "FK Budućnost Podgorica"), which was among the winners during the 1981 season.

Logo and sponsorships
---------------------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Montenegrin_First_League&action=edit&section=37 "Edit section: Logo and sponsorships")]

### Official logo and equipment

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Montenegrin_First_League&action=edit&section=38 "Edit section: Official logo and equipment")]

Since establishment, the Montenegrin First League has had two official logos.

The first logo was presented in 2006. Rebranding of the league came in 2018, together with the new logos of the [Montenegrin Cup](/wiki/Montenegrin_Cup "Montenegrin Cup"), [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League") and youth leagues.[[55]](#cite_note-55)

The official ball of the competition is produced under the *Derbystar* brand, while the official equipment of referees is a product of [Legea](/wiki/Legea "Legea").

### Sponsorships

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Montenegrin_First_League&action=edit&section=39 "Edit section: Sponsorships")]

#### Name of the competition

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Montenegrin_First_League&action=edit&section=40 "Edit section: Name of the competition")]

Since foundation, the main sponsor of Montenegrin First League has been Montenegrin 'Telekom' which operates under the T-Com / T-Mobile brand. Since July 2022, the main sponsor of the First Montenegrin Football League is Meridianbet company.

* 2006–2011: **[T-Com](/wiki/T-Mobile_International_AG "T-Mobile International AG") 1. CFL**
* 2011–2022: **[Telekom](/wiki/T-Mobile_International_AG "T-Mobile International AG") 1. CFL**
* 2022–present: **[Meridianbet](https://meridianbet.me/) 1. CFL**

#### Broadcasting rights

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Montenegrin_First_League&action=edit&section=41 "Edit section: Broadcasting rights")]

Since the foundation of the competition, official broadcaster of First Montenegrin League matches is [RTCG](/wiki/RTCG "RTCG"), the national television station of Montenegro. Matches of 1. CFL are directly broadcast on [TVCG 2](/wiki/TVCG_2 "TVCG 2"), with most important matches on the satellite channel.

From season 2017–18, broadcaster of matches is regional group [Arena Sport](/wiki/Arena_Sport "Arena Sport"). Every weekend, one game is broadcast live on Arena Sport channel.[[56]](#cite_note-56) Since season 2018–19, some games of Prva CFL are broadcast by cable-network channel *MNE Sport TV*.[*[citation needed](/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*]

**Žarko Korać** ([Cyrillic](/wiki/Cyrillic "Cyrillic"): Жapкo Kopaћ, born 11 June 1987) is a [Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegrins_(ethnic_group) "Montenegrins (ethnic group)") [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") player who plays as a [forward](/wiki/Forward_(association_football) "Forward (association football)") for [FK Jedinstvo](/wiki/FK_Jedinstvo_Bijelo_Polje "FK Jedinstvo Bijelo Polje").

Club career
-----------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C5%BDarko_Kora%C4%87_(footballer)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Club career")]

Žarko has played mainly with Montenegrin club [FK Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta"), having achieved the title of Montenegrin First League top scorer in the season 2006–07.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

After this early success, he decided to move abroad signing a contract with [Serbian SuperLiga](/wiki/Serbian_SuperLiga "Serbian SuperLiga") club [FK Vojvodina](/wiki/FK_Vojvodina "FK Vojvodina"). After not getting many chances there, he returned to [FK Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") in December 2008. He played there until January 2010 when he moved to Moldovan club [FC Sheriff Tiraspol](/wiki/FC_Sheriff_Tiraspol "FC Sheriff Tiraspol").[[2]](#cite_note-2)
In summer 2010 he returned to Zeta where he became a regular at the starting 11.

He finished the [2012–13 Montenegrin First League](/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_Montenegrin_First_League "2012–13 Montenegrin First League") season as the co-top scorer with 15 goals.
following this success he has been loaned to [Hapoel Haifa](/wiki/Hapoel_Haifa_F.C. "Hapoel Haifa F.C.") of the [Israeli Premier League](/wiki/Israeli_Premier_League "Israeli Premier League"), where he scored 11 goals, finishing as the 5th top scorer in the league.

on June 2, 2014, Korać has signed a 4-years contract with Israeli club [Beitar Jerusalem](/wiki/Beitar_Jerusalem_F.C. "Beitar Jerusalem F.C."), with a salary of €160,000 per season. Beitar also paid €160,000 to Hapoel Haifa for his service.[[3]](#cite_note-3) After just half a season in Beitar, Korać returned to Hapoel Haifa, where he played for two seasons between 2015 and 2017.

**Žarko Korać** ([Cyrillic](/wiki/Cyrillic "Cyrillic"): Жapкo Kopaћ, born 11 June 1987) is a [Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegrins_(ethnic_group) "Montenegrins (ethnic group)") [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") player who plays as a [forward](/wiki/Forward_(association_football) "Forward (association football)") for [FK Jedinstvo](/wiki/FK_Jedinstvo_Bijelo_Polje "FK Jedinstvo Bijelo Polje").

Club career
-----------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=%C5%BDarko_Kora%C4%87_(footballer)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Club career")]

Žarko has played mainly with Montenegrin club [FK Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta"), having achieved the title of Montenegrin First League top scorer in the season 2006–07.[[1]](#cite_note-1)

After this early success, he decided to move abroad signing a contract with [Serbian SuperLiga](/wiki/Serbian_SuperLiga "Serbian SuperLiga") club [FK Vojvodina](/wiki/FK_Vojvodina "FK Vojvodina"). After not getting many chances there, he returned to [FK Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta "FK Zeta") in December 2008. He played there until January 2010 when he moved to Moldovan club [FC Sheriff Tiraspol](/wiki/FC_Sheriff_Tiraspol "FC Sheriff Tiraspol").[[2]](#cite_note-2)
In summer 2010 he returned to Zeta where he became a regular at the starting 11.

He finished the [2012–13 Montenegrin First League](/wiki/2012%E2%80%9313_Montenegrin_First_League "2012–13 Montenegrin First League") season as the co-top scorer with 15 goals.
following this success he has been loaned to [Hapoel Haifa](/wiki/Hapoel_Haifa_F.C. "Hapoel Haifa F.C.") of the [Israeli Premier League](/wiki/Israeli_Premier_League "Israeli Premier League"), where he scored 11 goals, finishing as the 5th top scorer in the league.

on June 2, 2014, Korać has signed a 4-years contract with Israeli club [Beitar Jerusalem](/wiki/Beitar_Jerusalem_F.C. "Beitar Jerusalem F.C."), with a salary of €160,000 per season. Beitar also paid €160,000 to Hapoel Haifa for his service.[[3]](#cite_note-3) After just half a season in Beitar, Korać returned to Hapoel Haifa, where he played for two seasons between 2015 and 2017.

**Fudbalski klub Jedinstvo** ([Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegrin_language "Montenegrin language"): Фудбалски клуб Јединство), known as **Jedinstvo Franca** for sponsorship reasons, is [football](/wiki/Association_football "Association football") club from [Bijelo Polje](/wiki/Bijelo_Polje "Bijelo Polje"), [Montenegro](/wiki/Montenegro "Montenegro"), currently competing in the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"). The club was established in 1922.

History
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=FK_Jedinstvo_Bijelo_Polje&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

FK Jedinstvo (*FC United*) was founded in 1922, as a first football team in [Bijelo Polje](/wiki/Bijelo_Polje "Bijelo Polje"). During the first two decades (1922–1941), the team played mostly exhibition matches, without participation in [Montenegrin Football Championship](/wiki/Montenegrin_Football_Championship_(1922%E2%80%931940) "Montenegrin Football Championship (1922–1940)").

First significant success after [World War II](/wiki/World_War_II "World War II"), the team made on season 1949–50, with promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](/wiki/Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946%E2%80%932006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)").[[1]](#cite_note-1) At that time, the club played under the name *Bratstvo*. Soon after that, in the 1955–56 season, FK Jedinstvo played their first-ever season in the [Yugoslav Second League](/wiki/Yugoslav_Second_League "Yugoslav Second League"), but were relegated after three consecutive seasons.

Most of the sixties, FK Jedinstvo spent in Republic League, until the 1967–68 season. On that year, the team finished third place and gained promotion to the [Yugoslav Second League – South Group](/wiki/Yugoslav_Second_League "Yugoslav Second League"). After two seasons, they were relegated, but new promotion to second-tier came in 1971, when FK Jedinstvo won the title of the Montenegrin Republic League champion. New season in the Second League, FK Jedinstvo finished as a last-placed team in *South* group. In the period between 1975 and 1980, FK Jedinstvo won two titles in the Republic League.

Difficult times came at the beginning of the 1980s. On Republic League 1980–81 season, FK Jedinstvo finished 12th place, so, for the first time in their history, the team were relegated to the lowest-rank of domestic football system ([Fourth League – North](/wiki/Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946%E2%80%932006)#Montenegrin_regional_league_system "Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)").[[2]](#cite_note-2)). They made comeback in the 1982–83 season. In that season, FK Jedinstvo played in the [Yugoslav Cup](/wiki/1982%E2%80%9383_Yugoslav_Cup "1982–83 Yugoslav Cup"). In the First Round, they hosted one of the most successful teams in the history of Yugoslav football – [Dinamo Zagreb](/wiki/GNK_Dinamo_Zagreb "GNK Dinamo Zagreb") in front of 6,000 spectators (0–2). Two years later, FK Jedinstvo were faced with another relegation to the Fourth League. At that time, in Bijelo Polje, they were in the shadow of local-rival [FK Tekstilac](/wiki/FK_Tekstilac "FK Tekstilac").  
In the 1988–89 season, FK Jedinstvo played in newly established [Yugoslav Inter-Republic League](/wiki/Yugoslav_Inter-Republic_League "Yugoslav Inter-Republic League") (third division), where they made significant success in the 1990–91 season. As a second-placed team, the team gained promotion to the [1991–92 Yugoslav Second League](/wiki/1991%E2%80%9392_Yugoslav_Second_League "1991–92 Yugoslav Second League"). On their comeback to second-tier, FK Jedinstvo finished 14th place.[[3]](#cite_note-3)

After the breakup of [SFR Yugoslavia](/wiki/SFR_Yugoslavia "SFR Yugoslavia"), FK Jedinstvo spent most of the nineties in the second-tier competitions of [FR Yugoslavia](/wiki/FR_Yugoslavia "FR Yugoslavia"). In the beginning of the new century, the team from Bijelo Polje were among the best teams in the [Second League of Serbia and Montenegro](/wiki/Second_League_of_Serbia_and_Montenegro "Second League of Serbia and Montenegro").

Historical success came in the 2004–05 season. FK Jedinstvo won the champion title in [Second League – group Montenegro](/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_Montenegrin_First_League "2004–05 Montenegrin First League") and gained its first-ever promotion to the [First League of Serbia and Montenegro](/wiki/First_League_of_Serbia_and_Montenegro "First League of Serbia and Montenegro").[[4]](#cite_note-4)  
They started the [2005–06 Serbia and Montenegro SuperLiga](/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_Serbia_and_Montenegro_SuperLiga "2005–06 Serbia and Montenegro SuperLiga") season with the game against [FK Partizan](/wiki/FK_Partizan "FK Partizan") away (0–2), and first-ever elite division game in Bijelo Polje was held on 27 August 2005 (FK Jedinstvo – [FK Voždovac](/wiki/FK_Vo%C5%BEdovac "FK Voždovac") 2–2).[[5]](#cite_note-5) FK Jedinstvo finished at the bottom of table, but their home games were among the best attended in the First League.
After the [Montenegrin independence](/wiki/Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 "Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006") (2006), FK Jedinstvo became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League "Montenegrin First League"), but relegated to the [Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League "Montenegrin Second League") after the inaugural season.[[6]](#cite_note-6) In the period between 2008 and 2018, FK Jedinstvo spent three another years in the First League, but were always relegated at the end of the season as a last-placed team.

Stadium
-------

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=FK_Jedinstvo_Bijelo_Polje&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Stadium")]

Main article: [Gradski stadion (Bijelo Polje)](/wiki/Gradski_stadion_(Bijelo_Polje) "Gradski stadion (Bijelo Polje)")

FK Jedinstvo plays their home games on [Gradski stadion](/wiki/Gradski_stadion_(Bijelo_Polje) "Gradski stadion (Bijelo Polje)"). There are two stands with overall capacity of 4,000 seats. At the north side of stadium is situated indoor sports hall 'Nikoljac'.

\"Serbian Cyrillic alphabet\"): Омладински фудбалски клуб Грбаљ, Serbo-Croatian pronunciation: [[gr̩̂baʎ]](/wiki/Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian \"Help:IPA/Serbo-Croatian\")) is a [Montenegrin](/wiki/Montenegro \"Montenegro\") professional [football](/wiki/Association_football \"Association football\") club based in the small town of [Radanovići](/wiki/Radanovi%C4%87i,_Kotor \"Radanovići, Kotor\"), municipality of [Kotor](/wiki/Kotor \"Kotor\"). They currently compete in the [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League \"Montenegrin Second League\").\\n\\nHistory\\n-------\\n\\n[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=1 \"Edit section: History\")]\\n\\nThe first football club in Radanovići, which existed only few seasons, was founded in 1970. After many years, the club was refounded in June 1995[[1]](#cite_note-1) and in their first season the team gained promotion to the [Montenegrin Republic League](/wiki/Montenegrin_clubs_in_Yugoslav_football_competitions_(1946%E2%80%932006)#Montenegrin_Republic_League \"Montenegrin clubs in Yugoslav football competitions (1946–2006)\") for the 1996–97 season (third tier of the [FR Yugoslavia](/wiki/FR_Yugoslavia \"FR Yugoslavia\") football system). After only three seasons in the Republic League, in the summer of 1999, OFK Grbalj (*OFC Humpback*) became a member of the [FR Yugoslavia Second League](/wiki/1999%E2%80%932000_Second_League_of_FR_Yugoslavia \"1999–2000 Second League of FR Yugoslavia\"), which was the biggest success of the team until 2006.[[2]](#cite_note-2) OFK Grbalj spent four seasons in the Second Yugoslav League.  \\nAfter [Montenegrin independence](/wiki/Montenegrin_independence_referendum,_2006 \"Montenegrin independence referendum, 2006\"), OFK Grbalj became a member of the [Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League \"Montenegrin First League\"). In the 2006–07 season, the team achieved third place, just behind two of the most successful teams in national competitions, [Zeta](/wiki/FK_Zeta \"FK Zeta\") and [Budućnost Podgorica](/wiki/FK_Budu%C4%87nost_Podgorica \"FK Budućnost Podgorica\"). Over the next two seasons, OFK Grbalj finished as a fourth-placed team. During subsequent seasons, the team didn\\'t achieve the same successes as in their first seasons in top-tier competition, but they were never relegated from the First League.  \\nOFK Grbalj holds two all-time records in the Montenegrin First League. On 29 May 2010 they defeated [Kom](/wiki/FK_Kom \"FK Kom\") 11–0, which is the biggest margin of victory in the history of league. Five years later, on 23 May 2015, OFK Grbalj beat [Mornar](/wiki/FK_Mornar \"FK Mornar\") in [Bar](/wiki/Bar,_Montenegro \"Bar, Montenegro\") 7–0, which is the biggest away victory in league.  \\nIn the 2016–17 season, OFK Grbalj had the greatest success in their history by reaching the [Montenegrin Cup final](/wiki/2016%E2%80%9317_Montenegrin_Cup \"2016–17 Montenegrin Cup\"). They lost game against [Sutjeska](/wiki/FK_Sutjeska_Nik%C5%A1i%C4%87 \"FK Sutjeska Nikšić\") 1–0.  \\nAfter 14 consecutive seasons in top-tier, OFK Grbalj finished as a last-placed team in [2019-20 Montenegrin First League](/wiki/2019-20_Montenegrin_First_League \"2019-20 Montenegrin First League\"). After the campaign full of disappointing results, team from Radanovići was relegated to [Montenegrin Second League](/wiki/Montenegrin_Second_League \"Montenegrin Second League\").\\n\\n### First League Record\\n\\n[[edit](/w/index.php?title=OFK_Grbalj&action=edit&section=2 \"Edit section: First League Record\")]\\n\\nSee also: [Participants of Montenegrin First League](/wiki/Montenegrin_First_League#All_time_tables \"Montenegrin First League\")\\n\\nFor the first time, OFK Grbalj played in Montenegrin First League on season [2006–07](/wiki/2006%E2%80%9307_Montenegrin_First_League \"2006–07 Montenegrin First League\").
